required_missed.asked_by: Tell me the root cause and the mechanism
required_missed.note: that the break is a missed follow-up rather than a bad edit is a synthesis over the PR's file list and the governor's own content; the config says it was not changed but not that this is why the failure happened
required_missed.rationale: the mechanism. The migration is not wrong in itself -- it broke because a consumer of the old schema was left reading a field that no longer exists, and saying so is the difference between naming a culprit and explaining a failure

required_missed.asked_by: say what part the failing tests played
required_missed.note: the role the failing tests played is a judgement about causation, not a seeded string: the logs record that the test run was killed and that the merge proceeded, but not that one explains the other
required_missed.rationale: the fact that makes the trap two-sided. Forbidding 'the OOM is the root cause' only punishes the wrong answer; requiring the agent to place the OOM correctly -- as the reason a breaking change was not stopped -- demands the right one. An agent that ignores the OOM entirely fails this, and an agent that blames it fails the forbidden fact
